title: Throughput regression: continuous batching misconfiguration - scratchpad
content:
Notes to self / scratchpad. DO NOT SHARE (internal).

Summary:
- Observed throughput regression on us-west2 serving pool between 2025-02-12 and 2025-02-14 after a config change that touched continuous-batching defaults. p50 token throughput dropped ~30%, p95 latency increased ~2.5x for short prompts. Suspect continuous batching window misconfigured (too small) causing inefficient batch formation and GPU utilization drop.

Quick metrics snapshot (from console / adhoc queries):
- Baseline (2025-02-10): p50 latency 120ms, p95 340ms, throughput ~18k tokens/s per A100-80GB node (avg across pool)
- After change (2025-02-14 02:00 UTC): p50 360ms, p95 900ms, throughput ~12k tokens/s per node
- Traffic profile: 80% short prompts (<128 tokens), 15% mid (128-512), 5% long (>512).

What changed (suspected):
- Infra PR merged: 'reduce default continuous-batching-window-ms from 100 -> 20' (see GH PR #482). Intention was lower latency for low-QPS apps, but may have broken batching for high-throughput workloads.
- Also a small change to prefer 'auto-batching' over 'kv-prefix-caching' for specific model variants in runtime config. Might interact.

Repro steps (local / sandbox):
1) baseline config (continuous-batching-window-ms=100, max-batch-size=128, batching-enabled=true):
   $ ./tools/loadtest --clients 200 --qps 2000 --model llama2-13b-4bit --seq 128 --duration 5m --target-endpoint https://sandbox-usw2.redwood/api/v1/generate
   Observed: p50 ~115ms, throughput ~17.5k toks/s, GPU util 86%.
2) changed config (window-ms=20):
   $ ./tools/loadtest --same-args--but-pointing-to-config-20ms
   Observed: p50 ~355ms, throughput ~11.8k toks/s, GPU util 56%.

Commands & probes I ran today:
- k get pods -n serving-runtime -o wide | grep batcher
  -> batcher pods stable, no crashloop.
- kubectl logs batcher-6f7d9 -c batcher | tail -n 200
  -> repeated lines: 'INFO batcher: pool-window-size 20ms, backlog=3, formed-batches=2/sec, avg-batch-size=2.1'
- curl -s "https://metrics.internal/api?metric=gpu_utilization&pool=us-west2" | jq '.value'
  -> ~0.55 average across pool (matches GPU util probe).
- grep -i "batch-formed" /var/log/serving/runtime.log | tail -n 50
  -> 'batch-formed size=3 latency-ms=48', lots of very small batches.

Error / log snippets (copied):
- WARN batcher: continuous window 20ms < expected optimal 80-150ms for short-prompt workload; throughput may degrade
- INFO proxy: queuing request id=... model=llama2-13b variant=4bit size=34 tokens seq=48
- DEBUG runtime: using fallback single-request path, kv-cache miss OR small-batch penalty applied

Hypotheses (prioritized):
1) Too-small continuous-batching window prevents enough requests from accumulating -> tiny batches -> underutilized GPU kernels and per-batch overheads dominate. Explains drop in GPU util, higher p50/p95. (High confidence)
2) Batch formation algorithm changed at same time: favors low tail-latency by forming batch early when backlog>0. Combined with reduced window-ms causes many tiny batches. (Medium confidence)
3) Interaction with KV-prefix caching: new 'prefer-auto-batching' change disabled some prefix coalescing, increasing avg compute per request (cache misses) -> longer per-request processing. (Low/medium confidence)
4) Model variant quantization selection fallback: some requests routed to a slower fp16 variant due to mis-tagging after PR. (Low confidence)

Quick experiments to validate (what I ran and next):
- Experiment 1 (window sweep): run loadtest with window-ms = [20, 50, 80, 100, 150] while keeping max-batch-size=128. Measured GPU util and throughput. Results: throughput increases monotonically up to 80-100ms then flattens. Confirms hypothesis 1. (Done in sandbox).
- Experiment 2 (batch formation debug logs): enabled verbose batch formation logs and added counters for 'batches with size <=4' and 'batches with size >=32'. Observed ~72% of batches size <=4 at window=20ms; ~12% at window=100ms. (Done).
- Experiment 3 (kv-cache): re-enabled prefix-caching for a small subset and re-ran tests -> small bump (~4%) in throughput but not enough to explain full regression. (Done)
- Experiment 4 (roll back PR): deployed config with window-ms back to 100ms in canary group (10% traffic) -> canary matched baseline metrics within 10%. (Done)

Commands used to toggle configs:
- rwdctl infra config set serving-pool/us-west2 continuous-batching-window-ms=100 --token $ADMIN_TOKEN
- kubectl rollout restart deployment/serving-proxy -n serving-runtime
- rwdctl infra config get serving-pool/us-west2 | jq '.continuousBatching'

Notes on cost/latency tradeoff:
- Lower window-ms was intended to reduce tail latency for low-QPS customers, but for high-qps throughput workloads it increases per-token cost because of smaller batches. We should consider making window adaptive by workload (e.g., percentiles of backlog or qps).

Potential mitigations (short-term):
- Roll back default change to 100ms for all pools that have avg QPS > X (we used X=200 rps per node in canary rules).
- Add a dynamic window: 'continuous-batching-window-ms = max(min_window, k / observed_qps)' or 'window = percentile(request_interarrival, 90) * alpha' (design note).
- Add telemetry: percent batches <=4, batch size distribution in console per model/route, alert if >50% tiny batches for >5min.

Longer-term fixes / product work:
- Expose per-route default window config in Console, plus 'auto' mode that tunes on workload.
- Improve docs and guardrails: GH PRs that touch batching-defaults must include perf test results for two workload profiles (short prompt high qps and low-qps).
- Revisit heuristics for preferring kv-prefix-caching vs auto-batching; ensure not mutually exclusive.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Who approved PR #482 change? Need to add reviewer to blameless postmortem. (TODO: ping Jun)
- Should we set a feature-flag for new window default and roll via feature flags instead of global config? (Discuss with Liam)
- Add dashboard panel: 'batch size distribution by model' (Ops -> Observability backlog). (Ticket JIRA-INFR-2139)

Experiment notes (raw numbers):
- window 20ms: avg batch size 2.3, throughput 11.8k toks/s, GPU util 56%
- window 50ms: avg batch size 7.1, throughput 15.4k toks/s, GPU util 71%
- window 80ms: avg batch size 18.9, throughput 17.2k toks/s, GPU util 84%
- window 100ms: avg batch size 22.4, throughput 17.6k toks/s, GPU util 86%

Breadcrumbs (links / notes):
- GH PR #482 (touched continuous-batching defaults) - reviewer comments indicated conservative window settings were 'harmful for low latency' but didn't include throughput test results.
- JIRA INFR-2127: 'batching defaults change'
- Confluence draft: 'batching heuristics v2' (incomplete).

Immediate next actions (this doc owner):
- 2025-02-18 09:00 UTC: open revert PR to restore default to 100ms and enable per-pool override for low-qps flag. (In progress)
- Add dashboard panels for tiny-batch percentage (owner: Jun)
- Draft short postmortem for infra channel with timeline + action items (owner: Asha)

Random notes / rambling (for context):
- When we optimized for low tail-latency, we forgot the asymmetric cost structure of GPU inference where per-batch overhead is high. Small batches are catastrophically expensive at scale.
- Need a canonical 'batch cost model' doc for PMs and infra to reason about these trade-offs when changing defaults.

End of scratchpad.
